newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee settles up sharply, but off highs.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee settles up sharply, but off highs.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices rebounded after two consecutive sessions of losses to end sharply higher on Friday, bolstered by speculative short-covering, market sources said.
The most-active May contract surged to a session high of 190.50, up 8.25, before a round of local long liquidation ahead of the weekend pared gains, traders said.
May delivery ended up 4.10 cents per lb, to 186.35 cents, after sinking to a low of 179.00. Spot March settled 3.00 cents higher, at 205.00 cents, while the rest finished up 4.80 to 6.00.

After plunging more than 10 percent the past two days, prices pulled back further Friday morning after failing to make their 5.00-7.00 higher due. But the May contract survived a test of key support at 179.00 cents per lb, inspiring some of the shorts in the market to take cover.
Although no fresh news emerged today, traders and analysts said the tight supply situation continued to buoy sentiment.

"This is the tightest supplies have been in about 25 years and we're not looking at any sizable harvests," Allendale Commodities analyst Jim Cordier said. "I think next week you are going to see the bulls reattach their horns."
Traders will be keeping an eye on the Green Coffee Association of New York's monthly inventory data due after Monday's close.
Most market participants expect a modest rise in stocks. In January, supplies of green coffee stored in U.S. warehouses rose by 15,000 60-kg bags to 1,342,000 bags, the GCA said.

After Friday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks grew for the seventh day in a row, reaching 44,983 60-kg bags as of March 13. There were an additional 27,946 bags pending grading, the exchange said.

Technically, traders said May delivery's settlement above 185.00 cents today was viewed as positive. Near-term resistance was seen toward Friday's high of 190.50, while large sell-stops were said to be lurking below support at 179.00.

Traders await the CFTC Commitment of Traders report due late Friday, which they said is likely to show a slight decrease in speculative long positions due mainly to long liquidation of the March contract ahead of its first notice day on Tuesday.

After Friday's close, Colombia announced it would increase its internal coffee price to a new high of 383,375 pesos per 125-kg load. Since Jan. 31, Colombia has raised its internal coffee price six times.
Turnover was estimated at 12,027 lots, compared with Thursday's official tally of 14,484 lots.
